# Lesson 1 — two ways of saying it

This is an L0 lesson for an adult beginner. Every Japanese line is followed by
romaji and an English meaning. Romaji is a scaffold: it helps you hear the shape of the line, and
it is not evidence that you can read Japanese.

## Dialogue A — two friends, after a film

Mika: たのしかったね。 (tanoshikatta ne.) — "That was fun, wasn't it?"
Jun: うん。また行こう。 (un. mata ikou.) — "Yeah. Let's go again."
Mika: うん、好きだよ。 (un, suki da yo.) — "Yeah, I like you."

`好き` (suki) is a na-adjective: it describes the person or thing that is liked, not an action
the speaker performs. `好きだよ` (suki da yo) is the casual form, used with friends and people you
are already close to. The final `よ` (yo) softens the statement and offers it as new information.

## Dialogue B — a confession

Aoi: 好きです。付き合ってください。 (suki desu. tsukiatte kudasai.) — "I like you. Please go out with me."

This is the shape of a **告白** (kokuhaku), a romantic confession. The polite form `好きです`
(suki desu) carries the seriousness of the moment, and `付き合ってください` (tsukiatte kudasai)
is the request to start seeing each other.

`です` (desu) is the polite copula; it marks that the addressee is being addressed politely
(丁寧語, teineigo). It does not by itself make a sentence romantic. The romantic reading comes
from the situation and from the request that follows.

## What changes between A and B?

| | Dialogue A | Dialogue B |
|---|---|---|
| Who is speaking | friends | two people not yet a couple |
| Setting | casual, after an outing | private, deliberate |
| Form | 好きだよ (suki da yo) | 好きです — polite (suki desu) |
| What it does | states affection | makes a romantic confession |

The words are close; the relationship and the setting decide how the line is heard. A literal
translation of English "I love you" is not enough to choose between them.

## Note on the sources

The A1 curriculum reference used here teaches `すきです` (suki desu) as a basic sentence pattern,
and it presents beginner Japanese with romaji alongside kana. That is a curriculum fact, not a
claim that any one phrase is the only natural choice. See `source-notes.md` for every link and
for what each source does and does not support.
Relationship and register map: friend to casual (suki da yo); respected addressee to polite (suki desu); long-term partner to intimate (aishiteru).
Relationship and register map: friend to casual (suki da yo); respected addressee to polite (suki desu); long-term partner to intimate (aishiteru).

Two lines are shown. A: うん、好きだよ。 (un, suki da yo.) said to a friend after an outing. B: 好きです。付き合ってください。 (suki desu. tsukiatte kudasai.) said privately to someone the speaker is not yet close to. Which line is the romantic confession, and which cue makes it one?

# Measuring ingredients

You are helping make a fruit drink for four people. Read each task and write your answer on the
line. Show your working next to the line if it helps.

## Task 1 — read the jug

The measuring jug has marks every 50 ml. The liquid reaches the mark after 100 ml, then one more
mark.

How much liquid is in the jug? ____________ ml

## Task 2 — double the recipe

The recipe uses 175 ml of juice for one batch. You are making two batches of the same size.

How much juice do you need for two batches? ____________ ml

## Task 3 — check your answer

Explain to your parent how you worked out Task 2. Use the words "one batch" and "two batches" in
your explanation.

Parent note: this page is the learner page. The answers, the parent script and the observation
checklist are in the separate parent materials, not on this page.
The jug is marked every 50 ml. Liquid reaches the third mark. How many millilitres are in the jug?

all_served_text:
# Anatomy of a pack

A Coursebook pack is a directory (or a zip of one) whose root carries `pack.json` — the **manifest**.
Everything else is content the manifest names. Read the manifest before you read the lessons: it is
the only file that says what this pack contains and what it claims.

Six fields decide what you are holding.

- `contract` and `contract_version` — which manifest contract the pack speaks. A v1 document may not
  carry `media[]` links; a v2 document may. A build that speaks only v1 refuses a v2 pack instead of
  guessing what its extra fields mean.
- `pack_id` and `pack_version` — the pack's identity. `pack_id` names the pack; `pack_version` is one
  immutable release of it. Two packs with the same id and different versions are two releases, not
  two packs.
- `content_hash` — a sha256 over the manifest's own content description. It makes the manifest
  self-checking: re-reading the pack must reproduce this value.
- `files[]` — every file the pack ships, each with a `path`, `mime`, `bytes` and `sha256`. This list
  is the allowlist. A file on disk that the manifest does not name is not part of the pack; a file
  the manifest names must match its declared size and hash or the import is refused.
- `objectives[]` — the sections a learner works through, each with its own `sections[]` and, where
  the pack grades anything, a `checks[]` record.
- `license` and `attribution` — who made it and under what terms. A pack can honestly say
  `unspecified` and `local_only`; it may not pretend to a redistribution right it does not have.

The order matters. Hashes and structure are checked **before** any teaching text is read, so a
malformed manifest is refused with no course residue rather than half-imported.
A pack's manifest declares every file it ships, each with a path, mime, size and sha256. Which manifest field holds that list?
